lines.japanese: 快適な朝、三日目。居間に下りると、小鳩が朝食の支度を済ませたところだった。
lines.english: Day three. Another pleasant morning. When I came downstairs, Kobato had just finished making breakfast.

lines.japanese: 相変わらず早起きだなあ。相変わらず良い子だなあ。そして相変わらず可愛いなあ。俺は食卓の前に腰を下ろすと、小鳩とふたり手を合わせていただきますをした。
lines.english: An early riser as always. A wonderful girl as always. And adorable as always. I sat at the table, and Kobato and I put our hands together, said our thanks, and began to eat.

lines.japanese: 今日の朝食もパンか。もしかして、きのう俺が誉めたからパン食にしてくれたのかな。そんな小鳩の気遣いに応えるため、パンの話題を振ってサンキュー俺パンがマジ大好きなんだぜアピールをすることにした。
lines.english: Bread again this morning. Had she served it because I praised it yesterday? To answer her thoughtfulness, I decided to raise the subject and demonstrate that THANK YOU I SERIOUSLY LOVE BREAD.

lines.japanese: よし、こんなときはタカシの出番だな。
lines.english: Good. This was a task for Takashi.

lines.japanese: 「そういえばネットで見たんだけど、パンケーキのパンって、食べるパンじゃなくてフライパンのパンらしいよ」
lines.english: “I read online that the *pan* in *pancake* means a frying pan, not *pan* as in our word for bread.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、そうなんだ」
lines.english: “Oh. Really?”

lines.japanese: はむはむ。
lines.english: Nibble, nibble.

lines.japanese: 「まあ、食パンの食っていうのは、もともとフライパンと区別するために付いたって説もあるしね。食べるパンって意味で」
lines.english: “Though there's also a theory that the Japanese term for sliced bread literally means ‘eating bread’ because it had to be distinguished from frying pans. Bread for eating, you see.”

lines.japanese: 「はー」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: はむはむ。
lines.english: Nibble, nibble.

lines.japanese: 「でもいちばん有名なのは、菓子パンに対して主食パンと呼ばれるようになったっていう説みたい」
lines.english: “But the best-known theory is that the name comes from ‘staple-food bread,’ to set it apart from sweet buns.”

lines.japanese: 「ほーほー」
lines.english: “Uh-huh.”

lines.japanese: はむはむ。
lines.english: Nibble, nibble.

lines.japanese: おかしいな。兄妹水入らずの場が形成されるはずなのに、小鳩からは生返事しか返ってこない。
lines.english: Something was wrong. This was supposed to be a quiet moment for brother and sister alone, yet Kobato gave me nothing but noncommittal noises.

lines.japanese: 「ど、どうしたんだ小鳩。パンにまつわる豆ちしきが若干おもしろくなかったのか。よしじゃあ次はマーガリン豆ちしきにしよう。えっと、ネットで見たんだけどね、マーガリンっていうのは元々……」
lines.english: “Wh-what's wrong, Kobato? Were those bread facts somehow less than fascinating? Good, then next we'll try margarine facts. Let's see. I read online that margarine was originally...”

lines.japanese: 「あっ……ええっ？　な、なに？」
lines.english: “Oh... What? Wh-what is it?”

lines.japanese: 弁に熱がこもって身を乗りだしたら、いきなり小鳩が聞きかえしてきた。あらら。どうやらテレビに夢中で、俺の話が耳に入っていなかったらしい。
lines.english: When I leaned forward, warming to my subject, Kobato abruptly asked me to repeat myself. Oh, dear. Apparently the television had absorbed her so completely that she had not heard a word.

lines.japanese: なんだ、俺の話がつまらないわけじゃなかったのか。ああ、びっくりした。だよな。俺のパン話、おったまげるほど面白いもんな、ははは。
lines.english: Oh, so my story wasn't boring her. Man, that gave me a scare. Well, of course. My bread talk's so interesting it'll blow your mind. Ha ha ha.

lines.japanese: んー、どれどれ？　俺の可愛い妹はいったい何を観てたんだ？
lines.english: Now, then. What could my adorable sister have been watching?

lines.japanese: 「あら、なんて素敵なんでしょうこの指輪。素敵ですねー、こんな指輪プレゼントされちゃったら、女性はみんなクラッときちゃいますよねー」
lines.english: “Oh, what a beautiful ring! Isn't it lovely? Any woman who received a ring like this would go weak at the knees.”

lines.japanese: １２月が始まって早や一週間。嘘くさい胸を張った局アナが、クリスマスシーズンを盛りあげるために日本中の女性を焚きつけていた。
lines.english: December was already a week old. A network announcer thrust out her suspiciously artificial chest and incited women across Japan in the name of whipping up Christmas excitement.

lines.japanese: 画面右上のテロップは「聖夜に彼氏と行きたい店特集」。小鳩が見とれていたのはこれみたいだ。接写されたプリンだかババロアだかが、光を反射しながらプルプル揺れてる。
lines.english: The caption in the upper right read: SPECIAL: PLACES TO GO WITH YOUR BOYFRIEND ON CHRISTMAS EVE. This seemed to be what had captivated Kobato. A close-up of something between custard pudding and Bavarian cream quivered in reflected light.

lines.japanese: カメラが引いていくと、朝だってのにバックは夜景。ハンサム風の男とお嬢様っぽい女がきらめくワイングラスをカッチンさせていた。
lines.english: The camera pulled back to reveal a nighttime cityscape despite the morning hour. A handsome-ish man and an heiress-ish woman clinked glittering wineglasses.

lines.japanese: 荒んだ大人であるところの俺はつい鼻白んでしまうが、穢れなき天使であるところの小鳩は、どうやらお目々を星にして夢見心地のご様子。
lines.english: As the jaded adult among us, I could not help recoiling a little. Kobato, the untainted angel, watched dreamily with stars in her eyes.

lines.japanese: そうかあ、小鳩もこういうのに憧れる年頃かあ。
lines.english: So Kobato had reached the age when she dreamed of such things.

lines.japanese: うーん、頭の中では誰とワイングラスをカッチンしてるのかなあ。気になるなあ。いけ好かない優男だったら嫌だなあ。さりとて不細工も嫌だなあ。お兄ちゃんが認めるような男じゃないと困りますよっ？
lines.english: Hmm. Whose wineglass was she clinking against hers inside that head? I wanted to know. I hoped it wasn't some insufferable pretty boy. Then again, I didn't want him to be ugly either. Any candidate would have to earn her big brother's approval!

lines.japanese: 「ん、んんっ」
lines.english: “Ahem.”

lines.japanese: まだ見とれている小鳩の意識を引くため、咳払いを入れてみた。ついでにエアーネクタイをぐいぐいと直す。
lines.english: To reclaim Kobato's attention from the screen, I cleared my throat. For good measure, I tugged repeatedly at an imaginary tie.

lines.japanese: 「アーなんだ、エー小鳩はその、すすす好きな男とかいるのか」
lines.english: “Ahem. Well. Kobato, do you, ah... h-h-have some boy you like?”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: テレビに顔を向けていた小鳩が、ぴくんと反応した。ぽっかり口を開けたまま固まっている。
lines.english: Kobato, whose face had been turned toward the television, twitched in reaction. She froze with her mouth hanging open.
“Wh-what...”

lines.japanese: 「なっ」
lines.english: “Wh—”

lines.japanese: 「な、ななななななんでとつぜん……」
lines.english: “Wh-wh-wh-why are you asking that all of a sudden...?”

lines.japanese: 「アーなんだその、深い意味はないんだが、エー悪いようにはしないからお兄ちゃんには正直に話してごらん」
lines.english: “Ahem. Well, I don’t mean anything by it. You can tell your big brother the truth. I won’t give you a hard time.”

lines.japanese: 「だ、だってそんなの、いな、いないし」
lines.english: “B-but I don't. There isn't anybody.”

lines.japanese: 「なっ、なぁーん！　なーにもー、ポッポはー。兄ちゃんにはえんりょしなくていいのよー」
lines.english: “Whaaat? Oh, Poppo. You don't have to hold out on Big Brother.”

lines.japanese: 「そそ、そんなこと言われても、居ないものはおらんです。ない袖は振れんとです」
lines.english: “Y-you can say that, but there isn't anybody. You can't give what you haven't got.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　マジかよテメ、フカシこいてんじゃねーだろな。んなこと言って、ほんとはイブの日にちゃっかりカッチンコする予定とかあんじゃねーの、このマセガキ」
lines.english: “Huh? Seriously? You'd better not be bullshitting me. You're not secretly planning to go clinky-clink with somebody on Christmas Eve, are you, you precocious little brat?”

lines.japanese: 「ち、違うよう……予定、だって予定って、いつもどおり……」
lines.english: “N-no... My plans are just... the same as always...”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、いつも通り？」
lines.english: “The same as always?”

lines.japanese: 「うん。去年だってお父さんお母さんと……うちのみんなで手作りケーキ食べたもん。たぶん、今年もそんなかんじ」
lines.english: “Yeah. Last year, I had homemade cake with Mom and Dad... with everybody in the family. This year will probably be like that too.”

lines.japanese: そうか。そういや毎年ここん家はそんな感じだったな。去年はたしか鷲介が出席したはずだ。
lines.english: Of course. Come to think of it, that was how Christmas went in this house every year. Shusuke had attended last year, if memory served.

lines.japanese: 「あー、そうだいねー。そんな感じだいねー」
lines.english: “Oh, yeahhh. That's right, then.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、いつもどおり」
lines.english: “Mm. The same as always.”

lines.japanese: 「そかー、いつも通りかー」
lines.english: “I see. Same as always.”

lines.japanese: 「うんっ。うん、うん」
lines.english: “Mm! Yeah.”

lines.japanese: ははは、まだまだホームパーティーが楽しいお年頃か。
lines.english: Ha ha ha. So she was still at the age when a family party sounded exciting.

lines.japanese: ああ、じゃあ恋愛やら恋人やらに憧れてはいるけど、まだその対象が見つからないってカンジなのかな。
lines.english: Ah. Perhaps she admired romance and relationships in the abstract, but had yet to find anyone who inspired those feelings.

lines.japanese: ふむふむ、なるほどね。うーん、それじゃあ可愛い妹がいつかちゃんとしたカッチンを嗜めるように、お兄ちゃんが予行練習などさせてあげるのもいいかもしれない。
lines.english: Hmm, hmm. I understood. In that case, perhaps her big brother ought to give his adorable sister a little rehearsal, so she would know how to conduct a proper clink when the time came.

lines.japanese: うん、予行練習。そういうことなら妹を誘っても不自然じゃないよな。不自然とか言うやつがヘンなんだよ。頭イカれてるんだよ。よし。
lines.english: Yes. A rehearsal. If that was the purpose, inviting my sister would be perfectly natural. Anyone who called it unnatural was the strange one. Out of his mind. Good.

lines.japanese: 「コヴァ……小鳩っ？」
lines.english: “Koba—Kobato?”

lines.japanese: しかし俺は声が裏返っていた。
lines.english: Yet my voice broke.
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: 「んんっ……エーまあそのね、エーなんといいますかですね」
lines.english: “Ahem... Well, you see. Ahem. How shall I put this?”

lines.japanese: 俺は平静を装ってパンにマーガリンなど塗りながら、さりげなく話題を切りだした。
lines.english: Trying to act calm, I casually brought it up while spreading margarine on my bread.

lines.japanese: 「そのパン、さっき表面もぬったのに裏側もぬるんだ……」
lines.english: “You already spread it on the front. Now you're doing the back too...?”

lines.japanese: 「エー冬はつとめて、なんて申しますように、我が家でもこうした朝のひとときはたいへん素晴らしいものだと思うのですが」
lines.english: “Ahem. ‘In winter, the early morning,’ as the old saying goes. And of course I consider these mornings together at home a very fine thing—”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、耳にもぬるんだ？　そこまでマーガリンでコーティングしたら、パンの味なんてしなくなっちゃうよ」
lines.english: “Wait, you're spreading it on the crust too? If you coat it in that much margarine, you won't taste the bread at all.”

lines.japanese: 「エーときにはですね、エー朝の食卓以外にもですね、マーこうして小鳩さんと語らう機会があっても然るべきではないかなとですね」
lines.english: “Ahem. And yet perhaps, from time to time, there ought to be opportunities for Miss Kobato and me to converse somewhere beyond the breakfast table—”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、あああの、ついてるついてる、マーガリン手にぬってる……」
lines.english: “Oh, oh, um—it's on you, it's on you! You're spreading margarine on your hand...”

lines.japanese: 「２４日ふたりでどっか出かけるか」
lines.english: “Want to go somewhere together on the twenty-fourth?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 俺が我に返ったら、今度は小鳩が呆然とした。
lines.english: When I came to my senses, it was Kobato's turn to stare blankly.

lines.japanese: 「どこかに……？」
lines.english: “Go somewhere...?”

lines.japanese: 「うん。叔父さん叔母さんとは、またべつの機会にパーティーするとしてさ。イブはふたりでちょっとシャレた店でも行って、美味しいものとか食べちゃおうぜ」
lines.english: “Yeah. We can have a party with Uncle and Auntie another time. On Christmas Eve, you and I can go somewhere a little fancy and eat something good.”

lines.japanese: だって１２月２４日は神様のバースデー前夜である前に──
lines.english: After all, before December twenty-fourth was the eve of God's birthday—

lines.japanese: 「──小鳩の誕生日だもん。そんぐらいの金ならあるから、俺が連れてったるよ」
lines.english: “—it's Kobato's birthday. I can afford that much. Let me take you out.”

lines.japanese: あ、あれ、返事がない……。
lines.english: H-huh? No answer...

lines.japanese: う、うん、まあそうだよな……小鳩ぐらいの歳になれば、ぼちぼち男兄弟と歩くの嫌がるものだもんな。こればっかりはどこの家でも同じだから仕方ない。そう、それだ。
lines.english: W-well, of course. At Kobato's age, girls started objecting to being seen with their brothers. It happened in every family. Nothing to be done about it. Yes. That was it.

lines.japanese: 「いく」
lines.english: “I'll come.”
“What...?”

lines.japanese: 「い、いくっ」
lines.english: “I-I'll come.”

lines.japanese: 「ええっ！」
lines.english: “What!?”

lines.japanese: 「い、いっちゃういっちゃう、私いっちゃう」
lines.english: “I'll come, I'll come! I'm coming!”

lines.japanese: 「えええええっ！」
lines.english: “Whaaaat!?”

lines.japanese: 可愛い妹が可愛い顔して過激な動詞を連呼するので、俺は思わずどぎまぎしてしまった。
lines.english: My adorable sister kept repeating an unexpectedly charged verb with an adorable expression, and I found myself flustered despite myself.

lines.japanese: いかんいかん、これじゃまるで俺の中に新たな人格・軽部狩男が宿ったみたいじゃないか。
lines.english: No, no. At this rate, it was as though a new personality—Karuo Karube—had taken up residence inside me.

lines.japanese: 「あ……でもえっと、いいの？」
lines.english: “Oh... But, um, is it really okay?”

lines.japanese: 「なな、なにが」
lines.english: “Wh-what do you mean?”

lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃんの予定とか」
lines.english: “Your plans.”

lines.japanese: 「俺の予定？」
lines.english: “My plans?”

lines.japanese: 「あ……あー、そーね、２４日ね。うん、まあイブだからね。そりゃね、そりゃ俺と過ごしたいって女子はいっぱいいるよね。まあでも小鳩のためだからね、まあ小鳩のためだから全部キャンセルしとくよね、うん」
lines.english: “Oh... Right. The twenty-fourth. Yes, well, it *is* Christmas Eve. Naturally, loads of girls want to spend it with me. But this is for Kobato. Yes. For Kobato, I'll cancel every last one.”

lines.japanese: 俺は適当なことを言った。
lines.english: I said whatever came to mind.

lines.japanese: 「うん、じゃあいくっ」
lines.english: “Okay. Then I'll go!”

lines.japanese: 小鳩は子供みたいに遠慮なく微笑んだ。
lines.english: Kobato smiled without a trace of reserve, like a little girl.

lines.japanese: 「よし、じゃあ決まりだ」
lines.english: “Good. Then it's settled.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩はご機嫌ソングを口ずさみながら、パンにジャムを塗りはじめた。
lines.english: Humming a happy little song, Kobato began spreading jam upon her bread.

lines.japanese: うん、喜んでもらえるなら誘ってよかった。いつかはどっかの家の王子さまに射抜かれて、あっけなく兄離れしてゆくのだろうけど、とりあえず今年はまだ俺が王子さまでいさせてもらおう。
lines.english: Good. If it made her this happy, I was glad I had asked. Someday a prince from some other house would pierce her heart and, just like that, she would outgrow her brother. For this year, at least, she could let me remain her prince.

lines.japanese: 「ま、さすがに、夜景の見えるレストランでワインをカチンは無理だけどな」
lines.english: “Though a restaurant overlooking the city, with wineglasses going clink, is probably out of the question.”

lines.japanese: 「へう？　わいんおかちん？」
lines.english: “Hew? Wine go clinky?”

lines.japanese: なにそれ顔で目をぱちくりしてる。ひどい、冗談の解説なんてしたくないのに。
lines.english: She blinked at me with a face that plainly said *what are you talking about?* How cruel. I did not want to explain my own joke.

lines.japanese: 「いや、だっていまテレビで……」
lines.english: “But they just showed it on television...”

lines.japanese: 「え……あれ、いま小鳩なに観てた？」
lines.english: “Wait... What were you watching, Kobato?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、うん。えへへ、パリのぱてぃ、ぱてぃしえ？　の作ったプリンなんだって。一度でいいから食べてみたいねー」
lines.english: “Oh. Hee hee. They said the pudding was made by a Parisian pasty—pastry chef? I'd like to try it just once.”

lines.japanese: そっちかよ。
lines.english: *That* was what she had been staring at.

lines.japanese: 思わずフライングクロスチョップツッコミを入れたくなったが、手がマーガリンまみれだったので我慢した。
lines.english: I nearly answered with a flying cross chop, but my hands were covered in margarine, so I restrained myself.

lines.japanese: 通学路の途中にあるレトロなたばこ屋。
lines.english: The old-fashioned tobacco shop on my route to school.

lines.japanese: 三年間いままで気にも留めなかったけど、クラスメイトがいると分かったら何となく覗きたくなってしまう。繰りかえすが、俺の中の５分の４は友情に餓えているのだ。
lines.english: I had paid it no attention in three years. Yet the moment I learned a classmate lived there, I found myself wanting to peek in. I repeat: four-fifths of me was starved for friendship.

lines.japanese: 俺は道行くひとたちが見向きもしないガラス窓の前に立った。
lines.english: I stopped before the glass window every other passerby ignored.

lines.japanese: 「あっ」
lines.english: “Ah.”

lines.japanese: 俺の影がガラスに映ると、細い指が窓台にかかった。一瞬きのう見た老婦人かと思ったけど、病人のように白い肌には皺ひとつ見られない。顔は突っ伏したままだけど、間違いない、山科京だ。
lines.english: When my shadow fell across the glass, slender fingers appeared upon the sill. For an instant, I mistook her for the elderly woman I had seen yesterday, but there was not a wrinkle on that sickly white skin. Her face remained lowered, yet there could be no mistake. Miyako Yamashina.

lines.japanese: 「おはよう山科さん！　今日も薔薇色かい？」
lines.english: “Good morning, Yamashina! Is today rose-colored for you too?”

lines.japanese: 唸るような声が返ってきた。って、そんな姿勢で、ひどい接客態度だな。俺、客じゃないけど。
lines.english: A groan answered me. And in that posture, too. Terrible customer service—though I wasn't a customer.

lines.japanese: 「おいおいどうしたー、元気ないじゃないか」
lines.english: “Come now, what's wrong? You don't look very lively.”

lines.japanese: 「ていうか、俺が誰だか分かってる？　同じクラスの羽田ことスーパー委員長だけど」
lines.english: “Do you even know who I am? Haneda, your classmate and Super Class Representative.”

lines.japanese: 「ひょっとして具合悪いのか？　家のひと呼んでこようか？」
lines.english: “Are you feeling sick? Want me to go get someone from your family?”

lines.japanese: 「次『んー』って言ったらそっちの負けね。責任ボール山科さんからだぞ」
lines.english: “Whoever says ‘mmm’ next loses. The ball is in your court, Yamashina.”

lines.japanese: なんだこれ。山科京ってこんなキャラだったっけ？　いや、どんなキャラかよく知らないけど。
lines.english: What was this? Had Miyako Yamashina always been like this? Not that I knew what she was normally like.

lines.japanese: 三年間同じクラスだったとは言っても、直接話したのなんて数えるほどだったし。タカシの俺が言うのもなんだけど、山科京も山科京でかなり影の薄い子だったからな。
lines.english: We might have shared a class for three years, but we had spoken directly only a handful of times. Takashi was hardly one to talk, but Miyako Yamashina had an exceptionally faint presence of her own.

lines.japanese: などと考えていたら、山科京はいつの間にか上体を起こしていた。額をガラス窓の横べりに預け、壁に寄りかかるようにしながらこちらを見上げている。
lines.english: While I considered this, Miyako Yamashina had somehow raised her upper body. Resting her forehead against the edge of the glass, she leaned against the wall and looked up at me.

lines.japanese: い、いや、そんな死にそうな目で見つめられても困るんだけど……。
lines.english: I-I mean, what am I supposed to do when you stare at me like you're about to die...?

lines.japanese: 「めちゃめちゃしんどそうだな。大丈夫か……？」
lines.english: “You look absolutely miserable. Are you all right...?”

lines.japanese: 体が弱くて欠席が多いことぐらいは知ってるけど、いったいどんな病気なんだろう。この様子じゃ今日も学校は休み──
lines.english: I knew only that she was frail and often absent. What illness did she have? In this condition, she would surely miss school again today—

lines.japanese: 「そうだ山科さん、連絡事項があった。あのな、受験前の忙しい時期に悪いんだけど、クラス全員参加で卒業文集の制作作業をしなくちゃいけないんだ」
lines.english: “Right, Yamashina. I have an announcement for you. Sorry to bother you during this busy pre-exam period, but the whole class has to help produce the graduation anthology.”

lines.japanese: 「それでおととい班分けをしたんだけど、山科さんは俺の班になったから。以降シクヨロぴょん。自慢だが、我が羽田班はいずれ名だたる精鋭のみが集められた最強集団だ。共に働けることを光栄に思ってくれ」
lines.english: “We divided into groups the day before yesterday, and you were assigned to mine. Nice ta do biz with ya, bunnykins. Not to boast, but the Haneda Group is a mighty company of elites destined for fame. Consider yourself honored to work beside us.”

lines.japanese: 「や、山科さん？」
lines.english: “Y-Yamashina?”

lines.japanese: 「と、とにかくそういうわけだから、一度打ち合わせもしたいんだよ。次はいつ学校に来られそうだ？」
lines.english: “A-anyway, that's the situation, and we need to hold a meeting at least once. When do you think you'll be able to come to school?”

lines.japanese: 駄目だ。まるで話が噛みあわない。
lines.english: No use. We were not communicating in the slightest.

lines.japanese: 「そっか……悪いな、ツライとこ声かけちゃって。俺はやめようって言ったんだけど、俺が友達には挨拶するもんだって言って聞かなかったんだ」
lines.english: “I see... Sorry to bother you when you're feeling awful. I said we shouldn't, but I insisted that people ought to greet their friends and simply wouldn't listen to myself.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあな。えーと、行ってきます」
lines.english: “See you. Er... I'm off.”

lines.japanese: 手を上げて背を向けたとき、ふと湿った声が耳に触れた気がした。
lines.english: As I raised a hand and turned away, I thought a damp little voice brushed my ear.
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: なんか言ったか、あいつ？　ちょっと後ろを振りかえってみたけど、もう山科京は崩れおちてしまったのか、姿が見えなくなっていた。
lines.english: Had she said something? I looked back, but Miyako Yamashina had perhaps slumped down again, for she was already out of sight.

lines.japanese: 風邪薬でも飲んで眠かったのかもしれないな。まあ伝えることは伝えたしいいか。
lines.english: She might have taken cold medicine and grown drowsy. I had delivered the message, at least.

lines.japanese: ちょっと心配だけど、どうせ毎日通る道だ、気になるなら明日も明後日も覗いていけばいい。俺はいつもの通学路をやや早足で進んだ。
lines.english: I remained a little worried, but this was my route every day. If she stayed on my mind, I could peek in tomorrow and the day after as well. I resumed my familiar road to school at a slightly brisker pace.

lines.japanese: げっ。
lines.english: Gah.

lines.japanese: 昼休み。学食へ向かおうと階段を下ったら、俺が校内で会いたくないランキングのツートップが、揃って前方を歩いていた。
lines.english: At lunch, I descended the stairs toward the cafeteria and found the top two names on my list of People I Least Wanted to Meet at School walking together ahead of me.

lines.japanese: 「なー、渡来最近さー」
lines.english: “Hey, Watarai. Lately...”

lines.japanese: 「んー……なに？」
lines.english: “Hmm...? What?”

lines.japanese: 一人でも厄介なのが二人も……俺はげんなりして歩む速度が自然に落ちた。
lines.english: Either one was troublesome alone, and now there were two. My spirits sank, and my pace naturally slowed.

lines.japanese: 「羽田の雰囲気、ずいぶん変わったじゃん」
lines.english: “Haneda's whole vibe has changed a lot, right?”

lines.japanese: げっ、俺の話かよ！　しかも、俺たちの完璧な統合に疑念が向けられている！？
lines.english: Gah! They were talking about me! Worse, they were casting suspicion upon our flawless integration!

lines.japanese: 「そうかなあ？　あんなもんだよね」
lines.english: “Has it? He's always been like that, hasn't he?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、変わったって。なんつーの、あいつ自分から率先してクラス仕切るようなやつじゃなかったじゃん」
lines.english: “No, he's changed. I mean, he was never the sort to take charge of the class on his own.”

lines.japanese: 「さあ？　知らないよ、いままで猫かぶってただけじゃない？」
lines.english: “Who knows? Maybe he was just hiding his true nature before.”

lines.japanese: おお、渡来明日香よ、なんていいやつだ。本当は俺が変わったことを誰よりも疑っているくせに、この場はバックレかましてくれるというのか。
lines.english: Oh, Asuka Watarai, what a fine person you were! Though she doubted my transformation more than anyone, she was playing dumb for me here.

lines.japanese: あいつ、もしかしたらいいやつなのかもしれない。俺はちょっとやつを見直した。そうだよ、だから言ってるじゃない、渡来さんはとても素敵なひとなんだよ。
lines.english: Perhaps she was a good person after all. My opinion of her rose slightly. Yes, I keep telling you: Watarai is a wonderful person.

lines.japanese: 俺の中の明日香さまファンがひとりで力説しているあいだ、高内昌子は高内昌子で、羽田鷹志はフヨフヨ天然ＢＯＹからキラキラ熱血ＢＯＹへ変貌したのだと説きつづけていた。
lines.english: While the Asuka devotee within me argued this case alone, Shoko Takanouchi continued expounding her theory that Takashi Haneda had transformed from Floaty Natural-Airhead Boy into Glittering Hot-Blooded Boy.

lines.japanese: 「なに、羽田って渡来と二人のときはいつもあーなん」
lines.english: “What, does Haneda always act like that when he's alone with you?”

lines.japanese: 「うんそう」
lines.english: “Yeah.”

lines.japanese: 渡来明日香は適当な返事をしていた。
lines.english: Asuka Watarai answered carelessly.

lines.japanese: 「私、基本的にＭだから」
lines.english: “I'm basically a masochist, after all.”

lines.japanese: すごく適当な返事をしていた。
lines.english: She answered extremely carelessly.

lines.japanese: 「従順な雌奴隷だよね」
lines.english: “His obedient little slave girl.”

lines.japanese: ものすごく適当きわまる返事をしていた。
lines.english: Her answer reached the absolute extreme of carelessness.

lines.japanese: そしてそれらを鵜呑みにしてるっぽい高内昌子も大概だと思った。
lines.english: And Shoko Takanouchi seemed to be swallowing it whole, which said plenty about her too.

lines.japanese: 「はー、尽くす女ってやつ？　やっぱ羽田はセージュン系か」
lines.english: “Oh, the devoted-woman type? Guess Haneda really does like 'em sweet and innocent.”

lines.japanese: 「うん。彼の前では私、おしっこしない設定になってるから」
lines.english: “Yeah. The character I play for him doesn't even pee.”

lines.japanese: 「すげぇー、渡来おまえよくそんなん耐えられんな」
lines.english: “Wow. Watarai, it's amazing you can live like that.”

lines.japanese: 耐えてない耐えてない。つーか、付きあってない付きあってない。
lines.english: She isn't enduring anything. And we aren't dating, either.

lines.japanese: とても追いこす気にはなれず、俺は窓ガラスに額を付けて、しばらく直角三角形のオブジェと化していた。
lines.english: I could not bring myself to overtake them, so I pressed my forehead to the window and spent a while as an installation in the shape of a right triangle.

lines.japanese: 放課後。卒文制作作業のため、渡来明日香と二人きりになった。
lines.english: After school, I found myself alone with Asuka Watarai to work on the graduation anthology.

lines.japanese: クラスの男子たちが、去り際チラチラと様子をうかがっているのが分かった。ええ、替われるものならいくらでも替わりたいところですよ。
lines.english: As the boys left the classroom, I saw them repeatedly glancing our way. Believe me, gentlemen: if I could trade places with any of you, I gladly would.

lines.japanese: もっとも、俺がよくても渡来明日香は頑として譲らないだろう。彼女は俺というか俺たちに興味津々なのだ。悪い意味で。
lines.english: Even if I agreed, however, Asuka Watarai would stubbornly refuse. She was intensely interested in me—or us. In the worst possible sense.

lines.japanese: 「ねえ、偽物」
lines.english: “Hey, impostor.”

lines.japanese: 「なにー、化け物」
lines.english: “What is it, monster?”

lines.japanese: 「化け物って。女の子に向かってそれは傷つくよね」
lines.english: “Monster? That's a hurtful thing to say to a girl.”

lines.japanese: 「そうか！　ははは、男の子に向かって偽物もけっこう傷つくぞう！」
lines.english: “Is that so? Ha ha ha! 'Impostor' is a fairly hurtful thing to say to a boy too!”

lines.japanese: 「羽田君に会わせて」
lines.english: “Let me see Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「だから言ってるだろう、俺羽田ガハハ鼻毛ボーン」
lines.english: “As I keep telling you: me Haneda, haw haw, nose hair—boom!”

lines.japanese: 「認めない！」
lines.english: “I refuse to accept it!”

lines.japanese: 「認めなくてもいいからさ、とりあえず偽物ってのは勘弁してくれないかな。人前でそんな呼び方されると恥ずかしいんだよ」
lines.english: “You don't have to accept it. But could you stop calling me an impostor? It's embarrassing when you do that in front of people.”

lines.japanese: あ、検討してる。
lines.english: Ah. She was considering it.

lines.japanese: 明らかに「羽田君」でない者を羽田君とは呼びたくないが、いま「羽田君」だと主張しているこの羽田君の尊厳もおろそかにはしたくないのだろう。根はいいやつだ。
lines.english: She did not want to call someone plainly not ‘Haneda’ by that name. Yet neither, apparently, did she want to trample the dignity of this Haneda who presently claimed it. She was good at heart.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、ぱね田」
lines.english: “Then... Paneda.”

lines.japanese: それが妥協点か。
lines.english: That was her compromise?

lines.japanese: 「まあ、いいだろう。あだ名っぽいから当面それで良しとしよう」
lines.english: “Very well. It sounds sufficiently like a nickname. We shall use it for the time being.”

lines.japanese: 「で、ぱね田くん、今日の作業はなにをすればいいの」
lines.english: “So, Paneda, what are we working on today?”

lines.japanese: 「そうだな。今日はひとまず、班内での分担を決めるつもりだったんだが……」
lines.english: “Let's see. I intended to assign the work within the group today, but...”

lines.japanese: 「山科も針生先輩もいないよね」
lines.english: “Yamashina and Haryu aren't here.”

lines.japanese: 「残念だね」
lines.english: “What a shame.”

lines.japanese: 「解散だね」
lines.english: “Guess we're done.”

lines.japanese: 俺と渡来明日香はさっさと教室を引きはらい、たまたま方向が同じだったから駅まで一緒に帰った。途中、なんとなくゲーセンに寄っていった。一時間くらい。ガンシューを教えてやったらハマッてた。
lines.english: Asuka Watarai and I promptly vacated the classroom. We happened to be going the same way, so we walked to the station together. On a whim, we stopped at an arcade for about an hour. I taught her a light-gun game, and she got hooked.

lines.japanese: 店を出たあと面白かったかと聞いたら「羽田君と来たかったな」なんてしみじみ言うものだから、俺は例によって「俺羽田ガハハ」と答えて、そんで例によってぴしゃりと怒られた。
lines.english: Outside, I asked whether she had enjoyed it. She said wistfully, ‘I wish I'd come with Haneda.’ As usual, I answered, ‘Me Haneda, haw haw,’ and, as usual, she snapped at me.

lines.japanese: そんで別れ際、彼女の背を見送りながら例の５分の１の意識を前面に出して、ごめんね渡来さんと呟いた。世界が平和でありますように。
lines.english: As we parted, I watched her back recede, brought that familiar one-fifth of my awareness to the surface, and murmured, ‘I'm sorry, Watarai.’ *May peace prevail on Earth*.
